==== inheritedMembersAndIndexSignaturesFromDifferentBases.tlua (4 errors) ====
    -- ported from tests/cases/compiler/inheritedMembersAndIndexSignaturesFromDifferentBases.ts
    -- dropped: @target: es2015 and @strict: false directives (tlua defaults to latest target and strict checking); implicit-any members were made explicit
    
    -- note: tlua number keys and string keys are distinct domains, so a number-keyed member is only
    --   checked against a number index signature. Upstream additionally compares the numeric property 0
    --   against A's string indexer (JavaScript coerces numeric keys to strings); those TypeScript-only
    --   diagnostics are intentionally absent here, so F reports one error and G reports two.
    
    -- indexer in B is a subtype of indexer in A
    interface A {
        [s: string]: {
            a: any;
        };
    }
    interface B {
        [s: number]: {
            a: any;
            b: any;
        };
    }
    interface C {
        m: {};
    }
    
    interface D extends A, B, C { } -- error because m is not a subtype of {a;}
              ~
!!! error TLUA2411: Property 'm' of type '{}' is not assignable to 'string' index type '{ a: any; }'.
    
    interface E {
        0: {};
    }
    
    interface F extends A, B, E { } -- error because 0 is not a subtype of B's number indexer {a; b;}
              ~
!!! error TLUA2411: Property '0' of type '{}' is not assignable to 'number' index type '{ a: any; b: any; }'.
    
    interface G extends A, B, C, E { } -- two independent errors: m against the string indexer and 0 against the number indexer
              ~
!!! error TLUA2411: Property '0' of type '{}' is not assignable to 'number' index type '{ a: any; b: any; }'.
              ~
!!! error TLUA2411: Property 'm' of type '{}' is not assignable to 'string' index type '{ a: any; }'.
    
    interface H extends A, F { } -- Should report no error at all because error is internal to F
